newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-EL KASS RESCUES ZAMALEK'S BLUSHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EL KASS RESCUES ZAMALEK'S BLUSHES.

text.p: Veteran Ahmed El Kass saved African champions Zamalek from an embarrasing start to the defence of their African Champions' Cup title in the weekend's first round, first leg ties.
The 30-year-old Egypt international scored in the last five minutes to give the Cairo club a face-saving 2-0 win against minnows St George of Ethiopia at home on Friday night.

Zamalek's strikers were kept at bay for 75 minutes before Mohammed Sabry scored but it was El Kass's goal that gave the defending champions some respectability in a match they were expected to dominate.

But a stuttering start to this year's three African club competitions was not restricted to Zamalek. Several other of the fancied contenders also failed to make a big impression on the opening weekend.
South Africa's Orlando Pirates, who were African champions two years ago, squandered myriad opportunities against Roma Rovers of Lesotho on Saturday.

Pirates, playing at Johannesburg's Soccer City for the first time after a year-long ban by the Confederation of African Football (CAF), won only 1-0 despite almost total domination and continual attack.
CAF Cup holders Kawkab Marrakesh will take a slender 1-0 lead to Senegal for the second leg of their tie against ASC la Linguere.
A second-half penalty by Youssef el Amrani on Saturday might not prove enough in the Moroccan club's bid to hold on to their title.
Tunisia's Etoile Sahel, winners of the CAF Cup in 1995 and beaten finalists last year, were at the receiving end of a surprise 3-0 thumping in the African Cup Winners' Cup.
They went down to Etoile Filante of Burkina Faso in Ouagadougou on Sunday and face elimination.
Cup Winners' Cup holders Arab Contractors failed to score in their opening match away in Nairobi against Kenyan newcomers Mumias Sugar.
But the Egyptian team will be pleased with the goalless draw as they have home advantage in the return match against the Sugarmen, playing in African club competition for the first time.
There were more positive results from some of the other potential favourites for this year's trophies.

Ivorians Africa Sports won 3-0 at home against Ascot of Chad on Sunday while Jonas Ogandaga scored twice to help Moroccans Raja Casablanca to beat Sonacos de Diourbel of Senegal 3-1 in the Champions' Cup.

Both Nigeria's Julius Berger and Jomo Cosmos of South Africa won 3-0 away in their Cup Winners' Cup matches while Tunisia's Esperance had the weekend's biggest triumph, beating ASKO Kara 7-0 in the CAF Cup.
The CAF Cup game between AS Bantous of Zaire and Chad's Aslad Moundou in Kinshasa did not go ahead after the referees from the Central African Republic failed to turn up.
